constructs: unit testing with React Testing Library
codebase_expectations: React components are colocated with their unit tests using React Testing Library
Express routes have typed request/response interfaces; no implicit any on req.body
PostgreSQL queries go through the shared query builder; raw SQL only in reviewed migration files
Tailwind class names follow the project's token convention; no arbitrary values without a design review comment
Every new page-level component has a Storybook story before it merges

laddering_chains.attribute_quote: Mid engineers here ship features end to end — they don't hand off a PR to someone else to deploy. If you built it, you see it through to production.
laddering_chains.consequence: Feature ownership at the mid level requires comfort with the full vertical slice: React UI, Express route, database query, and the deploy itself
laddering_chains.value: End-to-end ownership reduces handoff friction and speeds time-to-production

stories.situation: A mid engineer finished a React feature and submitted the PR but marked it as blocked, waiting for a backend engineer to create the API route it needed.
stories.action: The tech lead paired with them to show how to create the Express route with typed interfaces, write the migration, and deploy the full feature together in one day.
stories.outcome: The engineer shipped their next three features end-to-end without pairing; velocity increased significantly over the following sprint.
stories.moral: The team invests in helping mid engineers grow into the full vertical slice; candidates who are not curious about the backend half of the stack will plateau faster here than they might expect.

work.summary: The team is building a B2B SaaS product as a Rails-style monolith using Node.js and React. Mid engineers own full features vertically: React component, API route, database change, and deployment. The codebase is straightforward enough that a focused mid engineer can hold the whole feature in their head without a platform team abstracting away the infrastructure. This makes onboarding fast but also means there is nowhere to hide — the candidate must be comfortable in both the UI and the database.

laddering_chains.attribute_quote: We write tests the same day as the code — it's not a separate phase. If you can't test it the day you write it, the feature isn't done.
laddering_chains.consequence: TDD or same-day test writing is a team norm, not a preference; PRs without tests are returned
laddering_chains.value: Test coverage as a confidence multiplier for the single-monolith architecture

codebase.summary: The codebase is a TypeScript monolith: React on the frontend, Express on the backend, sharing types through a shared package. Unit tests use React Testing Library for components and Jest for business logic. Storybook stories are required for page-level components before merging. The monolith is intentional — the team believes premature service extraction costs more than it saves at their current scale.

laddering_chains.attribute_quote: I want someone who is honest about what they don't know but curious enough to figure it out rather than blocking. Mid-level here means resourceful, not expert.
laddering_chains.consequence: The team values intellectual curiosity and resourcefulness over depth in any single area; candidates who block on gaps rather than researching them will feel friction
laddering_chains.value: Learning velocity as a differentiator for mid-level impact

bar.summary: The bar for mid-level is productive competence, not mastery: the candidate should be able to pick up a ticket in an unfamiliar part of the stack, research what they need, and deliver a working solution without requiring daily pairing. Accessibility is an explicit bar item — the team ships to enterprise customers who have WCAG 2.1 AA requirements in their contracts, so candidates who have never written aria attributes or tested with a screen reader will need to demonstrate they can learn quickly.

process.summary: Weekly sprints with same-day PR review as a team norm. No separate QA phase — engineers own quality end to end. Accessibility review is part of the PR checklist.

why.summary: The company is in active growth, shipping features at high velocity. Engineers have significant product influence at this stage — ideas surfaced in engineering are regularly incorporated into the roadmap.

team.summary: A team of four engineers, one designer, and one PM. Small enough that everyone knows what everyone else is working on; direct enough that feedback in PR comments is never softened to the point of ambiguity.

bars_overrides.base_anchor_text: Takes ownership of features from assignment to merge.
bars_overrides.override_anchor_text: Takes ownership of features from design to production deploy: creates the React component, the Express route, the migration, and deploys. Does not hand off to a backend engineer mid-feature. Asks for help when blocked rather than waiting silently.

bars_overrides.base_anchor_text: Writes readable, tested code that follows the team's conventions.
bars_overrides.override_anchor_text: Writes tests alongside the code on the same day — not as a follow-up PR. React Testing Library for component tests, Storybook story for any page-level component. Accessibility markup (aria-label, role, focus management) is part of the component, not an afterthought.

enriched_probes.probe_text: Walk me through the last feature you shipped end-to-end. What did the frontend change look like, what API route did you create or modify, and how did you deploy it?
Describe how you test a React component that fetches data from an API. What do you mock, what do you test for, and where does the Storybook story fit?

dealbreakers.label: Only comfortable with frontend; avoids backend work
dealbreakers.pattern: Candidate consistently hands off API and database work to backend-labelled engineers and has not independently shipped a database-touching route in recent experience
dealbreakers.job_relatedness_note: The role requires shipping full vertical slices without handoff; a candidate who avoids backend work cannot perform the core function of this mid-level role.
dealbreakers.evidence_quote: Mid engineers here ship features end to end — they don't hand off a PR to someone else to deploy.

red_flags.label: Has never worked with accessibility requirements
red_flags.evidence_quote: Accessibility review is part of the PR checklist; enterprise customers have WCAG 2.1 AA in their contracts.

consumer_slice.archetype: Fullstack engineer comfortable in both React and Node.js, with enough PostgreSQL depth to write and deploy their own database changes
disposition: Ships features end-to-end without splitting the work along frontend/backend lines
Writes tests the same day as the code
Honest about gaps and researches independently rather than blocking
consumer_slice.careerSignal: Has shipped multiple full-stack features in a TypeScript monolith including the database migration and deploy
redFlags: Only comfortable with the frontend half of a fullstack feature
dealbreakers: Refuses or is unable to write database-touching backend code
